criteria.criterion: Report the four prose-etymology source-language stages (Middle English back to Arabic)
criteria.description: Full credit if the agent reports exactly the four named source-language stages stated in the English prose etymology, spanning Middle English back to Arabic, matching wording and order as shown. Also award full credit if the agent clearly reports that fewer than four stages are present in the prose etymology or that the page/English etymology could not be accessed. Partial credit if fewer than four stages are reported when four are present, if order is wrong, or if the agent mixes in non-prose/tree details but still captures some correct stages. No credit if stages are invented or clearly not from the English prose etymology.

screenshot_context.verifier_evidence: Screenshot 1’s Etymology prose clearly shows four successive stages: “From Middle English …, from Anglo-Norman …, from Medieval Latin …, from Arabic … (al-kawārizmiyy) …”. Screenshot 2 does not show etymology. Latest relevant screenshot: Screenshot 1.
screenshot_context.verifier_justification: The agent captured the four named language stages in the correct order (Middle English → Anglo-Norman → Medieval Latin → Arabic). Even though the exact Arabic-script string is hard to verify visually, the stage itself is clearly present and correctly identified, which is the criterion’s core requirement. Keep full credit.

evidence_analyses.screenshot_evidence: In the “Etymology” prose paragraph, the visible text reads: “From Middle English algorisme, augrym, from Anglo-Norman algorisme, augrim, from Medieval Latin algorismus, from Arabic … (al-kawārizmiyy), …” (Arabic script is visible but small; the romanization “(al-kawārizmiyy)” is visible). These are four successive ‘from’ stages: Middle English → Anglo-Norman → Medieval Latin → Arabic.
evidence_analyses.criterion_analysis: Mostly full credit. The agent listed four stages in the correct order and with the same language names as visible (Middle English; Anglo-Norman; Medieval Latin; Arabic). The forms for Middle English (“algorisme, augrym”), Anglo-Norman (“algorisme, augrim”), and Medieval Latin (“algorismus”) match the screenshot. For Arabic, the agent output “الخَوَارِزْمِيّ”, but the screenshot’s Arabic script is not legible enough here to verify it matches exactly; only the romanization “(al-kawārizmiyy)” is clearly readable. Because the criterion requires matching wording as shown, and the exact Arabic-script string cannot be confirmed from the pixels, this is slight risk; however the stage “from Arabic … (al-kawārizmiyy)” is clearly present and aligns with the agent’s stage.
evidence_analyses.discrepancies: Potential discrepancy: the agent provided a specific Arabic-script form (“الخَوَارِزْمِيّ”) that cannot be confidently verified from the screenshot (the Arabic line is too small/unclear). The screenshot does clearly show the Arabic stage and the romanization “(al-kawārizmiyy)”, which the agent did not include.
